chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and life on the road
title: American fans and keeping her cool in noisy rooms
summary: At the New Orleans Hyatt-Regency, Dance marveled at her patience with talkative crowds and fans. Humes just smiles, gives autographs, and says she loves people.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Talking about spots where you played. We talked about European fans and we haven't said anything about American fans. But, I've often been around you, well like in New Orleans. What's the name of that hotel?
The Hyatt-Regency.
Yes, the Hyatt-Regency where I came at Mardi Gras and stayed with you, /remember?
Yes.

Well, I always marveled about how you, how patient and how you managed to keep a smile on and they're pie-eyed your face when customers would come up, /and they were talking while you were singing or something.
